data.reason: Frozen v1 E1–E6 first-pass assessment. PubMed's indexed primary-paper abstract, corroborating the Taylor & Francis publication DOI, describes pilots and non-pilots rating and comparing perceived urgency of five existing helicopter auditory alarms; pilots also ranked triggering-situation urgency. Human listeners, manipulated/contrasted alarm sound properties, perceived-urgency outcomes, experimental report methods and results in abstract, and publication before 2026-10-04 support inclusion to full-text screening only. Actual sound files, allocation, exact participant N, alarm levels, full Methods, numerical result extraction and independent sample identity were not reviewed. A single publication with multiple discovery paths is not multiple independent studies.
data.access_limitation: DOI 10.1080/0014013042000193282; publisher https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/0014013042000193282 returned 403 to direct web retrieval on 2026-11-10, so publisher-hosted abstract and full article were not directly read in this verification. Original journal-paper abstract was read in the [PubMed bibliographic record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15204277/) (PMID 15204277, Abstract section) on 2026-11-10, carrying the complete displayed abstract and publisher DOI, with 2004-06-22 issue date; full text remains unaccessed. Tool-mediated indexed public text; original HTTP Date/header, publisher article PDF, raw original abstract bytes/hash, audio and Methods/Results were not retained. DOI/publication identity already independently checked at source revision 1. No human review, numerical extraction, study/experiment/sample or full-text eligibility claimed. Original discovery HIT paths in source basis preserved.
